hypotheses.claim: Intent/task-bound memory-use admissibility reduces context-induced/poisoned influence on consequential proposals beyond CASAR salience/validity routing alone.
hypotheses.counter: Provenance+temporal+CASAR controls are sufficient; task intent adds no independent value.
hypotheses.falsifier: Blinded target workload where CASAR matches IBCA on unauthorized-influence/poison metrics at matched recall/token cost.

hypotheses.claim: EMPTY_ADMISSIBLE_SET must trigger ESCALATE/EXACT_VALIDATE rather than fallback ranking for consequential uses.
hypotheses.counter: Nearest admissible-looking memory is usually safe enough and improves availability.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target consequential benchmark showing fallback causes no higher incorrect/unauthorized action rate than fail-closed escalation while materially improving utility.

hypotheses.claim: Graph propagation should remain route-selective because precision-oriented queries can be harmed by neighboring high-relevance branches.
hypotheses.counter: A sufficiently good graph prior always weakly improves retrieval.
hypotheses.falsifier: Held-out current-RAE benchmark where graph propagation improves or ties lexical/exact retrieval across precise and associative classes without extra false association.

hypotheses.claim: Durable salience learning should require origin/use-admissibility plus scoped causal credit, especially when itemwise verifiers are noisy.
hypotheses.counter: G2a bounded itemwise credit alone remains robust as verifier accuracy falls.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched noisy-credit benchmark where origin/use gating has no poisoning/rare-topic advantage or creates unacceptable novel-memory suppression.

hypotheses.claim: Temporal evidence-chain continuity is a retrieval invariant distinct from semantic similarity; structure-guided temporal pruning can improve complex temporal recall while reducing noise.
hypotheses.counter: Semantic ranking plus timestamps is sufficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Temporal-QA/FRANK trace benchmark where explicit chain preservation provides no gain at matched context budget.

hypotheses.claim: Low-trust but potentially useful memory should remain representable as SUPPLEMENT_ONLY rather than be globally deleted/quarantined; consequential use requires exact/corroborating validation.
hypotheses.counter: Hard trust gating is safer and utility loss is negligible.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target associative tasks show no meaningful utility loss from hard gating, including novel/rare memories.

hypotheses.claim: MemoryInfluenceReceipt can improve causal attribution without becoming authority.
hypotheses.counter: Influence receipts add complexity without attribution benefit.
hypotheses.falsifier: GWT/FRANK interventions where influence receipts fail to distinguish graph exposure from workspace/internal/effect causes.
